assertion: By the 96th Congress of 1979-81, more than half the states (27) had split delegations, the highest share in the period we studied. From 1973 through 1994, there were never fewer than 20 split delegations in the Senate.

The dropoff in split delegations accelerated after the 113th Congress of 2013-15, when there were 17 (and for five months, 18). In the current Congress, which only has a few weeks left, only three states have split delegations.
There were just nine in the closely divided 84th Congress (1955-57), in which Democrats held a 49-47 majority.
